candidates.name: Cerebral abscess
support_spans: Noncontrast head CT demonstrated a hypodense area in the right basal ganglia with mass effect but no hemorrhage
Brain MRI revealed T2/FLAIR hyperintensity in the right basal ganglia and internal capsule with mild surrounding edema
Repeat MRI demonstrated progression with new involvement of the left basal ganglia, increased diffusion restriction, development of necrosis, and new peripheral contrast enhancement
candidates.why: The patient's symptoms and imaging findings are consistent with a cerebral abscess, which is a localized collection of pus in the brain.

candidates.name: Subacute bacterial endocarditis with septic emboli
support_spans: He was found minimally responsive and arrived febrile and intermittently responsive
Lumbar puncture yielded an opening pressure of 23 cm H₂O and slightly hazy cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) with 538 WBCs/mm³
Transthoracic echocardiography showed no valvular vegetations, but this does not rule out the possibility of septic emboli
contradict_spans: Transthoracic echocardiography showed no valvular vegetations
candidates.why: The patient's fever, altered mental status, and cerebrospinal fluid findings could be consistent with subacute bacterial endocarditis with septic emboli, although the absence of valvular vegetations on echocardiography makes this less likely.

candidates.why: The patient's cerebrospinal fluid findings and imaging results are consistent with a pyogenic brain abscess, which is a collection of pus in the brain caused by a bacterial infection.
